messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: P1 alert - tokyo-prod-1 - kv_cache fragmentation spike -> CUDA OOMs on inference nodes. Alerting on >50% slab fragmentation + 10+ CUDA malloc failures in 5m. Grafana: https://grafana.company/shot/ABCD1234 :rotating_light:
Maria: oncall here, ack. patching and triage starting. tagging infra and runtime.
Samir: I see a sudden uptick in continuous_batch_size_bytes and prefix fanout from the model rollout 2026-03-15T09:12UTC. keys/sec spiked 6x. likely continuous batching + longer seqs causing huge prefix KV entries.
Leila: can we throttle cont-batching quickly? there's a runtime flag we can flip per node: CONT_BATCHING_MAX_BYTES. set it to 8MB to stop runaway aggregation. also reduce MAX_CONCURRENT_BATCHES to 2.
Maria: good call. rolling a config patch to tokyo-prod-1 small pool (2 nodes) first. Nick please canary.
Nick: starting canary patch on nvidia-02 and nvidia-03 now. kubectl patch cmd below.
Nick: ```
# patch configmap runtime-config
kubectl -n inference patch configmap runtime-config -p '{"data":{"CONT_BATCHING_MAX_BYTES":"8388608","MAX_CONCURRENT_BATCHES":"2"}}'
# then rolling restart the inference daemonset on canary nodes
kubectl -n inference rollout restart ds/inference-runtime --selector=host=nvidia-02,nvidia-03
```
deploy-bot: Rolling restart initiated for ds/inference-runtime (canary nodes). rollout id: r-20260315-09-32.
ops-bot: Dumping top allocator stats from canary node nvidia-02:
```
arena_free: 1.2G
arena_total: 6.1G
slab_frag_ratio: 0.72
cuda_malloc_failures: 0 -> 0 after patch
kv_cache_entries: 54M -> trending down
```
Maria: immediate observation: fragmentation on canary dropped from 0.76 -> 0.48 within 90s of config flip. good sign.
Samir: also enabling kv-eviction-priority to LRU for affected pools helped reclaim ~600MB quickly. doing that cluster-wide in the next minute.
Leila: important: this is a symptomatic mitigation. root cause seems to be model rollout that increased typical request seq_len distribution (many long histories) + a bug in continuous batching which doesn't cap prefix share when fanout > 1. filing bug now.
Maria: CS Team - any customers impacted?
CS Team: We have 3 active sessions from enterprise customers in APAC; they reported 5-10% request errors between 09:10-09:28UTC. We're sending an incident note and offering a short postmortem.
Samir: proposed hotfix PR: short-term patch to runtime to enforce per-request KV cap and a safety throttle when cont-batch fanout > 2. will open PR and request review.
Leila: PR link: https://git.company/infra/cont-batching/pulls/432 - includes tests and metrics counters.
Maria: next steps: 1) finish cluster-wide config flip to CONT_BATCHING_MAX_BYTES=8MB 2) enable LRU eviction 3) roll back model rollout (if errors continue) 4) engage on-call allocator engineers for arena tuning.
Nick: cluster-wide patch applied to tokyo-prod pool. observing recovery: tail latency back to normal within 4 minutes. eviction churn stabilized.
deploy-bot: patch completed on 12 nodes. rollout id: r-20260315-09-37.
Maria: marking severity reduced to P2. will keep monitoring for 30m. anyone seeing remaining CUDA mallocs?
Samir: a few remaining malloc failures on two hosts; suspect leftover fragmented arenas. running on-host python diagnostic to trigger arena compaction: `python3 tools/arena_compact.py --force` on the two hosts.
Leila: note: we also toggled a PyTorch allocator knob on canary: `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=garbage_collection_threshold:0.6,max_split_size_mb:32` - helped avoid tiny split allocations that bloated fragmentation.
CS Team: customer update sent. they'll accept the workaround but asked for timeline on permanent fix.
Maria: handing off to night oncall at 09:58UTC. please take follow-ups: runbook updates (add CONT_BATCHING_MAX_BYTES alert), schedule postmortem, coordinate with model infra team re: rollout gating by seq_len distribution.
Samir: logging follow-up tasks: - revert cont-batching safety if we ship a code-level fix, - add histograms to trace keys-per-request, - implement safety throttle on fanout.
Leila: I'll own the allocator follow-up (arena reslice + thresholds) and the PR.
Nick: leaving canary notes: observed ~40% drop in eviction rate and recovery of CUDA OOMs to 0 after the change. attaching perf graphs in #incidents-postmortems.
Maria: thanks all. close thread once postmortem doc created. :white_check_mark:
